reference: Parity cases run the same script under system Bash and GNU tar from the runner reference PATH. Three static archive payloads are generated independently with Python standard-library tarfile in USTAR/PAX formats; GNU tar validates their expected listing, extraction, mode and link behavior. Archive bytes are not asserted because the documented contract excludes byte-identical tar/gzip encodings. The archive-name collision case intentionally observes GNU binding to the latest extracted pathname; it does not presume preservation of the original source inode data.
coverage: Traditional cf syntax, recursive creation, PAX long names, symlinks, listing, -O, and -C cwd restoration.
Independent USTAR extraction of regular, directory, symlink and hard-link entries.
Independent PAX path-record extraction for a basename beyond ustar limits.
Gzip tar create/list/extract and binary member output.
Failed -C cwd restoration, missing-member error status, hard-link creation semantics, and private FIFO archive behavior.
Regular hardlink creation for nonconflicting member names, recursive/PAX link targets, duplicate same-inode operands and strip-components link rewriting.
Archive-lifetime writer context across -C and repeated successful/failed calls.
Ordinary FIFO metadata creation/extraction, independent USTAR input, -p and default umask behavior.
Observe GNU-compatible late hardlink binding after an ordinary archive-name collision; this does not qualify preservation of source topology or data across collisions.
--same-owner/--no-same-owner/--numeric-owner owner restoration against GNU tar in the same unprivileged sandbox (H2); delayed directory times.
G39-G41: leading '/' removal and -P, uname/gname in headers, --exclude/--wildcards on extract, -S sparse members, --acls, --transform, --delete and --to-command, against GNU tar.

G111: -g/--listed-incremental level-0 and increments (GNU snapshot format 2, dumpdir members, renamed and swapped directories, deletion on -g /dev/null extraction), GNU-made incremental archives, -N/--newer/--after-date/--newer-mtime on create and list, and the incremental option diagnostics.
exclusions: Append/update, sparse formats, unsafe or absolute member/link paths, device nodes, and exact archive/compression bytes are not asserted.
Device-node parity is deferred pending an isolated synthetic mknod/stat fixture or reviewed syscall mock.

Only stable ordinary regular-file hardlinks and FIFO metadata are extended. Character/block devices, copy-mode special files, concurrent mutation, forward hardlinks, fault injection and exhaustive archive dialects remain outside this coverage.

Distinct source inodes mapped onto one archive pathname can make a later hardlink alias bind to the replacement data, as independently observed with GNU tar. General preservation of source data/topology across conflicting archive member names is not claimed.
Root's default owner restoration cannot be observed in the unprivileged sandbox; it shares the --same-owner path and is checked in the image as root.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata reports the registered tar loadable as a builtin; this checks shell integration, not GNU tar behavior.
cases.script: type -t tar

cases.purpose: Traditional tar cf syntax creates a recursive archive containing a long PAX path and symlink; GNU tar output, extraction tree, modes and -C working-directory restoration are compared. Archive bytes are removed because the documented contract excludes byte-identical encodings.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/nested restored
printf 'alpha\000omega\n' > source/data
printf longname > source/nested/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp
chmod 640 source/data
ln -s data source/link
before=$PWD
tar cf archive.tar -C source data link nested/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp
[[ $PWD == $before ]]
tar tf archive.tar
tar xf archive.tar -C restored
[[ $PWD == $before ]]
tar xOf archive.tar data
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Build the same archive after changing the input timestamp and confirm its extracted timestamp is the requested epoch.
cases.script:
mkdir src restored
printf 'same bytes\n' > src/member
touch -t 202001010000 src/member
tar --mtime=@0 -cf a.tar -C src member
touch -t 202001020000 src/member
tar --mtime @0 -cf b.tar -C src member
cmp a.tar b.tar || exit 1
tar -xf b.tar -C restored
stat -c %Y restored/member
rm a.tar b.tar

cases.purpose: Extracts a fixed USTAR archive encoded independently with Python tarfile, covering a directory, binary file, symbolic link and hard link; GNU tar listings and extracted filesystem/link relationships are the oracle.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > oracle.tar
tar -tf oracle.tar
tar -xf oracle.tar
tar xOf oracle.tar bundle/data
rm oracle.tar

cases.purpose: Reads a fixed POSIX PAX archive encoded independently with Python tarfile; its overlong path requires the PAX path record, and GNU tar supplies expected listing, stdout extraction, status and tree.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > oracle.tar
tar -tf oracle.tar
tar -xf oracle.tar
tar xOf oracle.tar 'nested/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp'
rm oracle.tar

cases.purpose: Creates, lists and extracts a gzip-compressed tar stream with a NUL-containing payload; GNU tar plus its gzip dependency is the reference, while archive bytes are removed because compression encodings may differ.
cases.script:
mkdir source restored
printf 'compressed\000fixture\n' > source/data
tar -czf archive.tar.gz -C source data
tar -tzf archive.tar.gz
tar -xzf archive.tar.gz -C restored
tar xzOf archive.tar.gz data
rm archive.tar.gz

cases.purpose: Checks GNU --strip-components path rewriting during extraction and verifies the selected member can still be read to stdout; the archive is removed so only resulting fixture files are compared.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/one/two restored
printf 'stripped payload\n' > source/one/two/value
tar -cf archive.tar -C source one/two/value
tar -xf archive.tar --strip-components=2 -C restored
tar xOf archive.tar one/two/value
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Checks GNU --no-recursion archives and extracts the named directory entry without its child tree; GNU tar listing and resulting tree define the expected behavior.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/child restored
printf leaf > source/child/data
tar -cf archive.tar --no-recursion source
tar -tf archive.tar
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Extracts the same independently encoded USTAR member once with default umask handling and once with -p under umask 077; GNU tar establishes both resulting file modes.
cases.script:
umask 077
printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > oracle.tar
mkdir default preserved
tar -xf oracle.tar -C default
tar -xpf oracle.tar -C preserved
rm oracle.tar

cases.purpose: Checks the documented -C restoration contract after a missing relative directory and records GNU tar statuses for both that failure and a missing -O member. The printed statuses are compared against GNU tar; the final process status is the -C failure status.
cases.script:
printf payload > data
before=$PWD
rc_c=0
tar -cf archive.tar -C missing data || rc_c=$?
[[ $PWD == $before ]] || exit 90
rm archive.tar
tar -cf archive.tar data
rc_m=0
tar -xOf archive.tar absent || rc_m=$?
rm archive.tar
printf 'failed-C:%s missing-member:%s\n' "$rc_c" "$rc_m"
exit $rc_c

cases.purpose: Archive two names for one regular inode and verify GNU-compatible extracted hard-link topology, with complete byte/mode/link tree comparison.
cases.script:
mkdir restored
printf shared > original
ln original twin
tar -cf archive.tar original twin
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Archive, list and extract only an ordinary private FIFO; GNU tar defines its metadata-only type and resulting tree.
cases.script:
mkfifo stream
tar -cf archive.tar stream
tar -tf archive.tar
mkdir restored
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Character and block device tar entries are outside the private regular-file fixture contract.
cases.reason: GNU parity for device-node headers needs a future disposable VM with an isolated synthetic mknod/stat fixture or reviewed syscall mock. Host device paths and raw-device access are explicitly out of scope; this case executes no command.

cases.purpose: An overlong first hardlink path requires PAX linkpath on a recursive alias. Archive a FIFO sibling too; both the builtin and independent GNU tar decode the result before full topology/mode/data comparison.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/nested restored independent
printf shared > source/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp
ln source/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp source/nested/twin
mkfifo -m 0640 source/nested/pipe
tar -cf archive.tar -C source pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp nested
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
/usr/bin/tar -xf archive.tar -C independent
[[ restored/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp -ef restored/nested/twin && independent/pppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppppp -ef independent/nested/twin && -p restored/nested/pipe && -p independent/nested/pipe ]]
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: Repeated regular operands emit GNU-compatible hardlink members without unlinking their own target; strip-components rewrites the hardlink name and target consistently.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/bundle restored
printf shared > source/bundle/original; ln source/bundle/original source/bundle/twin
tar -cf archive.tar -C source bundle/original bundle/twin bundle/original
tar -xf archive.tar --strip-components=1 -C restored
[[ restored/original -ef restored/twin ]]
tar -xOf archive.tar bundle/original
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: The writer remembers logical member names across -C changes, then starts a fresh hardlink context for another archive in the same shell.
cases.script:
mkdir first second restored one-member
printf shared > first/data; ln first/data second/alias
before=$PWD
tar -cf archive.tar -C first data -C ../second alias
[[ $PWD == "$before" ]]
tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
[[ restored/data -ef restored/alias && $PWD == "$before" ]]
tar -cf only.tar -C second alias
tar -xf only.tar -C one-member
[[ -f one-member/alias && $PWD == "$before" ]]
rm archive.tar only.tar

cases.purpose: A missing operand after a first hardlink member fails archive creation; the next same-shell archive remains self-contained and does not reference a prior archive path.
cases.script:
mkdir restored
printf shared > original; ln original twin
rc=0; tar -cf partial.tar original absent twin || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 2 ]]
tar -cf next.tar twin
tar -xf next.tar -C restored
[[ -f restored/twin ]]
printf 'first-status=%s\n' "$rc"
rm partial.tar next.tar

cases.purpose: Decode a fixed Python-authored USTAR FIFO and following regular member under umask077, once normally and once with -p. Following file creation verifies umask restoration.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | base64 -d > oracle.tar
mkdir default preserved
umask 077
tar -tf oracle.tar
tar -xf oracle.tar -C default
: > default/after-mask
tar -xpf oracle.tar -C preserved
: > preserved/after-mask
[[ -p default/pipe && -p preserved/pipe ]]

cases.purpose: Establish GNU writer behavior when a second inode replaces the first inode archive pathname before an alias of the first inode is written; decode with independent GNU tar.
cases.script:
mkdir first second restored
printf first-data > first/a
ln first/a first/alias
printf second-data > second/a
tar -cf archive.tar -C first a -C ../second a -C ../first alias
/usr/bin/tar -xf archive.tar -C restored
printf 'a=%s\nalias=%s\n' "$(<restored/a)" "$(<restored/alias)"
if [[ restored/a -ef restored/alias ]]; then printf 'topology=linked\n'; else printf 'topology=distinct\n'; fi
rm archive.tar

cases.purpose: H2: --same-owner makes extraction chown each member to the archived owner; as a non-root user a foreign uid fails with GNU's per-member diagnostic (file before its directory) and exit 2.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s out
printf hi > s/f
/usr/bin/chmod 4755 s/f
/usr/bin/touch -d @86400 s/f s
/usr/bin/tar --owner=12345 --group=12345 -cf other.tar s
tar --same-owner -xf other.tar -C out 2>/tmp/err || echo rc=$?
/usr/bin/sed 's/^.*tar: /tar: /' /tmp/err
/usr/bin/stat -c '%a %n' out/s/f

cases.purpose: H2: without --same-owner a non-root extraction does not chown (no diagnostics), and applies the umask (set-id bits dropped) unless -p.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s out
printf hi > s/f
/usr/bin/chmod 4755 s/f
/usr/bin/tar --owner=12345 --group=12345 -cf other.tar s
tar -xf other.tar -C out
/usr/bin/stat -c '%a %n' out/s/f
/usr/bin/mkdir p
tar -p -xf other.tar -C p
/usr/bin/stat -c '%a %n' p/s/f

cases.purpose: H2: the archived user/group names are used when they exist locally (here the runner's own), so chown succeeds; --numeric-owner uses the archived ids instead and fails for a foreign id.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s out num
printf hi > s/f
/usr/bin/touch -d @86400 s/f
/usr/bin/tar --owner=runner:12345 --group=runner:12345 -cf named.tar s/f
tar --same-owner -xf named.tar -C out && echo named-ok
tar --same-owner --numeric-owner -xf named.tar -C num 2>/tmp/err || echo rc=$?
/usr/bin/sed 's/^.*tar: /tar: /' /tmp/err

cases.purpose: H2: --no-same-owner after --same-owner turns owner restoration off again (the last option wins).
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s out
printf hi > s/f
/usr/bin/chmod 4755 s/f
/usr/bin/touch -d @86400 s/f s
/usr/bin/tar --owner=12345 --group=12345 -cf other.tar s
tar --same-owner --no-same-owner -xf other.tar -C out && echo quiet

cases.purpose: Directory times (and owners) are applied once the members inside the directory are extracted, so an archived directory keeps its modification time.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s/d out
printf hi > s/d/f
/usr/bin/touch -d @86400 s/d/f s/d s
/usr/bin/tar -cf d.tar s
tar -xf d.tar -C out
/usr/bin/stat -c '%Y %n' out/s out/s/d

cases.purpose: G40: tar -c of an absolute path stores it without the leading '/' (GNU's warning on stderr) and the archive extracts; -P keeps the '/' on create and list.
cases.script:
mkdir src; echo payload > src/f
tar -cf /tmp/a.tar "$PWD/src/f" 2>/tmp/err
/usr/bin/sed 's/^.*tar: /tar: /' /tmp/err
tar -tf /tmp/a.tar | /usr/bin/sed "s|^${PWD#/}|PWD|"
mkdir x; (cd x && tar -xf /tmp/a.tar) && echo extracted
tar -cPf /tmp/p.tar "$PWD/src/f" 2>/tmp/err; /usr/bin/wc -c < /tmp/err
tar -tPf /tmp/p.tar | /usr/bin/sed "s|^$PWD|/PWD|"
/usr/bin/rm -rf x/*

cases.purpose: G40: plain archives carry the owner's user and group names (ustar uname/gname), so tar -tv shows names, not ids.
cases.script:
touch plain
tar -cf /tmp/u.tar plain
/usr/bin/dd if=/tmp/u.tar bs=1 skip=265 count=32 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/tr -d '\0'; echo
/usr/bin/dd if=/tmp/u.tar bs=1 skip=297 count=32 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/tr -d '\0'; echo
tar -tvf /tmp/u.tar | /usr/bin/awk '{print $1, $2, $3, $NF}'

cases.purpose: G39: --exclude applies on extraction and listing; --wildcards makes member operands fnmatch patterns ('*.c' matches s/a.c).
cases.script:
mkdir s; touch s/a.c s/b.o
tar -cf /tmp/x.tar s
mkdir o1; tar -xf /tmp/x.tar -C o1 --exclude='*.o'; (cd o1 && /usr/bin/find . | /usr/bin/sort)
tar -tf /tmp/x.tar --exclude=a.c
mkdir o2; tar -xf /tmp/x.tar -C o2 --wildcards '*.c' || echo rc=$?
(cd o2 && /usr/bin/find . -type f | /usr/bin/sort)
tar -tf /tmp/x.tar --wildcards 's/*.o'
tar -tf /tmp/x.tar '*.c' 2>/tmp/err || echo rc=$?
/usr/bin/sed 's/^.*tar: /tar: /' /tmp/err

cases.purpose: G39: -S stores a file with an 512 KiB hole as a sparse member (small archive), tar -tv shows the real size, and extraction restores the hole and the bytes.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/truncate -s 512K sp; printf x >> sp
tar -cSf /tmp/sp.tar sp
[ $(/usr/bin/stat -c %s /tmp/sp.tar) -lt 65536 ] && echo small-archive
tar -tvf /tmp/sp.tar | /usr/bin/awk '{print $3, $NF}'
mkdir o; tar -xf /tmp/sp.tar -C o
/usr/bin/cmp sp o/sp && echo same
[ $(/usr/bin/stat -c %b o/sp) -le 64 ] && echo has-hole
tar -xOf /tmp/sp.tar | /usr/bin/wc -c
/usr/bin/rm -f sp o/sp

cases.purpose: G41: --transform/--xform rewrite member names with sed s expressions (flags g, x, number) on create and extract; a bad expression is a usage error.
cases.script:
mkdir s; touch s/f s/aaa
tar -cf /tmp/t.tar --transform='s,^s,p,' s/f
tar -tf /tmp/t.tar
tar -cf /tmp/u.tar --xform='s/a/b/2' --transform='s|s/|q/|' s/aaa
tar -tf /tmp/u.tar
tar -cf /tmp/g.tar s/aaa; mkdir o; tar -xf /tmp/g.tar -C o --transform='s/a/A/g;s,^s/,,'; /usr/bin/ls o
tar -cf /tmp/v.tar --transform='s/(f)/[\1]/x' s/f; tar -tf /tmp/v.tar
tar -cf /tmp/w.tar --transform=foo s/f 2>/tmp/err || echo rc=$?
/usr/bin/sed -n '1s/^.*tar: /tar: /p' /tmp/err

cases.purpose: G41: --delete removes the named members (and directory contents) in place; a missing member is reported with exit 2.
cases.script:
mkdir d; touch a b d/c
tar -cf /tmp/t.tar a b d
tar --delete -f /tmp/t.tar a d
tar -tf /tmp/t.tar
tar --delete -f /tmp/t.tar zz 2>/tmp/err || echo rc=$?
/usr/bin/sed 's/^.*tar: /tar: /' /tmp/err
tar -tf /tmp/t.tar

cases.purpose: G41: --to-command pipes each regular member to a sh -c command with TAR_FILENAME, TAR_SIZE, TAR_MODE and TAR_FILETYPE; a failing command is reported and tar exits 2.
cases.script:
mkdir d; echo abc > d/f; chmod 640 d/f; ln -s f d/l
tar -cf /tmp/t.tar d
tar -xf /tmp/t.tar --to-command='echo "$TAR_FILENAME $TAR_SIZE $TAR_MODE $TAR_FILETYPE"; /usr/bin/tr a-z A-Z'
tar -xf /tmp/t.tar --to-command='/usr/bin/cat >/dev/null; exit 3' 2>/tmp/err || echo rc=$?
/usr/bin/sed 's/^.*tar: [0-9]*: /tar: PID: /; s/^.*tar: /tar: /' /tmp/err

cases.purpose: G39: --acls stores POSIX ACLs as SCHILY.acl.access/default records and restores them on extract; without --acls none are restored.
cases.script:
echo q > q; mkdir dd
/usr/bin/setfacl -m u:$UID:rw q 2>/dev/null || exit 0
/usr/bin/setfacl -d -m u:$UID:rx dd
tar --acls -cf /tmp/q.tar q dd
mkdir o; tar --acls -xf /tmp/q.tar -C o
/usr/bin/getfacl -c -n o/q o/dd 2>/dev/null
mkdir n; tar -xf /tmp/q.tar -C n
/usr/bin/getfacl -c -n n/q 2>/dev/null

cases.purpose: G62: -d/--diff/--compare reports what differs on disk with GNU's words (Mod time, Size, Contents, Mode, Symlink, File type, Not linked to, Cannot stat/readlink) and exits 1 when anything differs, 2 for a member that is not in the archive.
cases.script:
run() { r=0; "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e || r=$?; /usr/bin/cat /tmp/o; /usr/bin/sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //' /tmp/e; echo "rc=$r"; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s/d; echo a > s/a; echo bb > s/b; /usr/bin/ln -s a s/l; /usr/bin/ln s/a s/h
/usr/bin/touch -h -d @86400 s/a s/b s/l s/d s
tar -cf /tmp/x.tar s
run tar -df /tmp/x.tar
run tar -dvf /tmp/x.tar
echo b > s/a; /usr/bin/touch -d @86400 s/a; run tar --diff -f /tmp/x.tar
echo zzzz > s/a; run tar --compare -f /tmp/x.tar
echo a > s/a; /usr/bin/touch -d @86400 s/a; /usr/bin/chmod 600 s/b; run tar -df /tmp/x.tar; /usr/bin/chmod 644 s/b
/usr/bin/rm s/l; /usr/bin/ln -s b s/l; run tar -df /tmp/x.tar
/usr/bin/rm s/l; run tar -df /tmp/x.tar; /usr/bin/ln -s a s/l
/usr/bin/rm s/b; /usr/bin/mkdir s/b; run tar -df /tmp/x.tar; /usr/bin/rmdir s/b
run tar -df /tmp/x.tar s/a
run tar -df /tmp/x.tar s/zz
run tar -d < /tmp/x.tar

cases.purpose: G62: -d reads a gzip archive (-z) and compares through -C.
cases.script:
run() { r=0; "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e || r=$?; /usr/bin/cat /tmp/o; /usr/bin/sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //' /tmp/e; echo "rc=$r"; }
/usr/bin/mkdir s o; echo a > s/a; /usr/bin/touch -d @86400 s/a s
tar -czf /tmp/x.tgz s
run tar -dzf /tmp/x.tgz
cd o; run tar -dzf /tmp/x.tgz -C ..; cd ..
echo c > s/a; run tar -dzf /tmp/x.tgz

cases.purpose: G62: -h/--dereference archives what symbolic links point to (a file, a directory's contents); a dangling link fails with exit 2.
cases.script:
run() { r=0; "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e || r=$?; /usr/bin/cat /tmp/o; /usr/bin/sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //' /tmp/e; echo "rc=$r"; }
/usr/bin/mkdir s; echo a > s/a; /usr/bin/ln -s s/a la; /usr/bin/ln -s s sl; /usr/bin/ln -s nowhere dang
tar -chf /tmp/h.tar la; tar -tvf /tmp/h.tar | /usr/bin/cut -c1-10
tar --dereference -cf /tmp/h2.tar la sl; tar -tf /tmp/h2.tar
tar -cf /tmp/p.tar la; tar -tvf /tmp/p.tar | /usr/bin/cut -c1-10
r=0; tar -chf /tmp/d.tar dang 2>/dev/null || r=$?; echo "dangling rc=$r"
/usr/bin/mkdir o; tar -xf /tmp/h.tar -C o; /usr/bin/cat o/la; test -L o/la || echo regular

cases.purpose: G62: --format=FORMAT and -H FORMAT write gnu, oldgnu and v7 headers as GNU tar does (magic, directory slash, ././@LongLink names, v7 limits and refusals); an unknown name is "Invalid archive format", exit 2.
cases.script:
run() { r=0; "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e || r=$?; /usr/bin/cat /tmp/o; /usr/bin/sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //' /tmp/e; echo "rc=$r"; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s/d; echo a > s/a; /usr/bin/ln -s a s/l; /usr/bin/touch -h -d @86400 s/a s/l s/d s
for f in gnu oldgnu v7 ustar; do
  tar --format=$f -cf /tmp/f.tar s/a s/d s/l; echo "$f"
  tar -tvf /tmp/f.tar | /usr/bin/cut -c1-10,32-
  /usr/bin/od -An -c -j257 -N8 /tmp/f.tar; /usr/bin/od -An -c -j512 -N100 /tmp/f.tar | /usr/bin/tr -s ' \\0' ' '
done
tar -H gnu -cf /tmp/h.tar s/a; /usr/bin/od -An -c -j257 -N8 /tmp/h.tar
tar --format posix -cf /tmp/p.tar s/a; tar -tf /tmp/p.tar
n=$(printf "n%0120d" 0); : > s/$n; /usr/bin/touch -d @86400 s/$n
tar --format=gnu -cf /tmp/L.tar s/$n; tar -tf /tmp/L.tar | /usr/bin/wc -c; /usr/bin/od -An -c -N16 /tmp/L.tar | /usr/bin/head -1
run tar --format=v7 -cf /tmp/v.tar s/$n
/usr/bin/mkfifo s/f; run tar --format=v7 -cf /tmp/v.tar s/f
run tar --format=bogus -cf /tmp/b.tar s/a
run tar -H bogus -cf /tmp/b.tar s/a
/usr/bin/mkdir x; tar --format=v7 -cf /tmp/v7.tar s/a s/d; tar -xf /tmp/v7.tar -C x; test -d x/s/d && echo v7-dir-extracted

cases.purpose: G62: fatal errors end with GNU tar's words and exit 2: not a tar archive, an archive that cannot be opened, a missing -C directory, and an archive cut short (Unexpected EOF in archive).
cases.script:
run() { r=0; "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e || r=$?; /usr/bin/cat /tmp/o; /usr/bin/sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //' /tmp/e; echo "rc=$r"; }
echo junk > j.tar; run tar -tf j.tar
: > e.tar; run tar -tf e.tar
run tar -tf nope.tar
echo a > a; tar -cf /tmp/a.tar a
/usr/bin/head -c 700 /tmp/a.tar > t.tar; run tar -tf t.tar
/usr/bin/mkdir o; run tar -xf t.tar -C o
/usr/bin/head -c 1024 /tmp/a.tar > n.tar; run tar -tf n.tar
run tar -xf /tmp/a.tar -C /nonexistent
r=0; tar -tzf j.tar 2>/dev/null || r=$?; echo "tzf junk rc=$r"
/usr/bin/rm -f t.tar n.tar

cases.purpose: G111: -g SNAPSHOT makes a level-0 dump (the snapshot names GNU's format 2) and two increments that store only changed files, with dumpdir 'D' members listed by -tvv -G (Y/N/D entries, R/T for a renamed directory, X and a temporary name for two swapped directories); extracting the three dumps with -g /dev/null deletes the files the increments no longer hold and leaves the dumped tree. Archives and snapshot live in /tmp: their times and inode numbers vary. Changes wait a clock tick after each dump: GNU takes a dump's start from the fine clock, so a change within the same coarse tick (the clock file times use) can look older than the dump.
cases.script:
TOUCH() { /usr/bin/touch -h -d "@$1" "${@:2}"; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s/a/b s/c s/old s/x s/y s/gone/sub
echo one > s/a/one; echo two > s/a/b/two; echo three > s/c/three; echo o > s/old/o
echo X > s/x/xf; echo Y > s/y/yf; echo g > s/gone/sub/g
TOUCH 86400 $(/usr/bin/find s)
/usr/bin/sleep 0.1
tar -cf /tmp/l0.tar -g /tmp/snap s
/usr/bin/head -c 15 /tmp/snap; echo
/usr/bin/sleep 0.1
echo more >> s/a/one; echo new > s/c/new; /usr/bin/rm s/c/three; /usr/bin/rm -r s/gone; /usr/bin/mv s/old s/renamed
TOUCH 172800 s/a/one s/c/new $(/usr/bin/find s -type d)
/usr/bin/sleep 0.1
tar -cf /tmp/l1.tar -g /tmp/snap s
/usr/bin/sleep 0.1
/usr/bin/mv s/x s/t; /usr/bin/mv s/y s/x; /usr/bin/mv s/t s/y; echo z > s/renamed/z
TOUCH 259200 s/renamed/z $(/usr/bin/find s -type d)
/usr/bin/sleep 0.1
tar -cf /tmp/l2.tar -g /tmp/snap s
for l in 0 1 2; do echo "== level $l"; tar -tvv -G -f /tmp/l$l.tar; done
/usr/bin/mkdir o; cd o
for l in 0 1 2; do tar -xf /tmp/l$l.tar -g /dev/null; /usr/bin/find . | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort; done
/usr/bin/cat s/a/one s/x/* s/y/*

cases.purpose: G111: two incremental archives made by GNU tar 1.35 (-g, gzip'ed: a level 0, then an increment that deletes and adds files, renames a directory and swaps two) are listed with -tvv -G (dumpdirs with X/R/T records) and extracted with -G over a tree holding extra files, which are deleted, with the renames applied.
cases.script:
printf '%s' '' | /usr/bin/base64 -d > /tmp/l0.tgz
printf '%s' '' | /usr/bin/base64 -d > /tmp/l1.tgz
tar -tvv -G -zf /tmp/l0.tgz; tar -tvv -G -zf /tmp/l1.tgz; tar -tzf /tmp/l1.tgz
/usr/bin/mkdir o; cd o; tar -xzf /tmp/l0.tgz -G
echo junk > s/d/junk; /usr/bin/mkdir -p s/d/jd/deeper; echo k > s/x/keep-not
tar -xzf /tmp/l1.tgz -G
/usr/bin/find . | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort; /usr/bin/cat s/x/* s/y/* s/d/f s/renamed/o

cases.purpose: G111: -N/--newer/--after-date DATE (data or status time) and --newer-mtime DATE (data time) on create keep directories and leave out older files ("file is unchanged; not dumped" with -v); a DATE starting with . or / names a file whose mtime is used; on -t only members not older than DATE are listed; GNU's "Treating date" note, unknown-date substitution and missing-file diagnostics.
cases.script:
run() { r=0; "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e || r=$?; /usr/bin/cat /tmp/o; /usr/bin/sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //' /tmp/e; echo "rc=$r"; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p n/sub; echo o > n/old; echo e > n/edge; echo m > n/sub/mid
/usr/bin/touch -d '2020-01-01 00:00:00' n/old; /usr/bin/touch -d '2021-01-01 00:00:00' n/edge ref
/usr/bin/touch -d '2022-06-01 00:00:00' n/sub/mid; /usr/bin/touch -d '2019-01-01' n/sub n
S() { /usr/bin/sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //' | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort; }
tar -cf /tmp/a.tar --newer-mtime=2021-01-01 n; tar -tf /tmp/a.tar | S
tar -cvf /tmp/b.tar --newer-mtime=./ref n 2>&1 | S
tar -cvf /tmp/b.tar --newer-mtime '2021-01-01 00:00:01' n 2>&1 | S
tar -cvf /tmp/c.tar -N 2030-01-01 n 2>&1 | S
tar -cf /tmp/c.tar --after-date=2021-01-01 n; tar -tf /tmp/c.tar | S
tar -cf /tmp/all.tar n
tar -tvf /tmp/all.tar --newer-mtime=2021-01-01 2>&1 | S
tar -tf /tmp/all.tar -N '2021-06-01 00:00:00' 2>&1 | S
run tar -cf /tmp/d.tar -N 'not a date' n
run tar -cf /tmp/d.tar -N ./missing n
run tar -cf /tmp/d.tar --newer=/missing n

cases.purpose: G111: GNU tar's checks of the incremental options: -g with -N, a bad --level, --level without -g (a warning; the archive is made), --level=0 forcing a full dump, and a dumpdir in an incompatible ustar archive.
cases.script:
run() { r=0; "$@" >/tmp/o 2>/tmp/e || r=$?; /usr/bin/cat /tmp/o; /usr/bin/sed 's/^[^ ]*: line [0-9]*: //' /tmp/e; echo "rc=$r"; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p s/d; echo a > s/a; echo b > s/d/b
run tar -cf /tmp/x.tar -g /tmp/s1 -N 2021-01-01 s
run tar -cf /tmp/x.tar -g /tmp/s1 --level=x s
run tar -cf /tmp/x.tar --level=1 s
tar -tf /tmp/x.tar | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort
run tar -cf /tmp/x.tar --format=ustar -g /tmp/s2 s
tar -cf /tmp/f0.tar -g /tmp/s3 s; tar -cf /tmp/f1.tar -g /tmp/s3 s; tar -tf /tmp/f1.tar
tar -cf /tmp/f2.tar -g /tmp/s3 --level=0 s; tar -tf /tmp/f2.tar

cases.purpose: Bash exposes tar as a builtin whose help documents the incremental (-g, -G, --level) and date (-N, --newer-mtime) options.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t tar) == builtin ]] || exit 1; h=$(help tar) || exit 1; for w in --listed-incremental -G/--incremental --level=0 --newer-mtime=DATE -N/--newer; do [[ $h == *"$w"* ]] || exit 1; done; printf 'tar builtin and documented help available\n'
cases.stdout: tar builtin and documented help available
